samples.summary: The new envelope validation is bypassed by the import/upload paths, which still forward any upstream body verbatim
samples.evidence:
The diff centralises the rule "only forward a body whose `error` is an object with a string `code`" for the six content/export sites. Four other command paths reach stderr with the *same* unvalidated pass-through the change was meant to eliminate:
- `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:164` — `io.stderr(JSON.stringify(res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }, null, 2))`
- `packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:194` — same line
- `packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:159` — same line
- `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:217` — same line
These hit the very same backend content endpoint (`PUT /documents/:id/content`, which `docs/design/cli.md:1029` documents as returning `TYPE_MISMATCH`), so an Express/Nest 404/500 body (`{message, error: "Not Found", statusCode}`) is non-null, skips the `??` fallback, and is printed as if it were the documented envelope — `error.code` reads `undefined`. Worse, `packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84` and `packages/cli/skills/slides-import-pptx.md:72` explicitly document `HTTP_ERROR` as the code agents branch on when "the server rejected the create or content PUT" — the exact case where the fallback does not fire. Fix belongs at these four sites (route them through `forwardUpstreamError`-equivalent logic, or an `isErrorEnvelope`-gated `io.stderr`).

samples.summary: Task doc's non-goal asserts other command paths "do not have this pattern"; files/upload.ts does
samples.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-45` scopes out "other command paths (sheets/cells/files) that do not have this pattern". `packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:215-219` does have exactly this pattern (`io.stderr(JSON.stringify(res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }...))`), as do the three import modules. The stated justification for the scope boundary is factually wrong about the repo, so a future reader will believe those paths were audited when they were not.

samples.summary: Sibling command paths still flatten the documented TYPE_MISMATCH envelope, leaving the envelope contract enforced unevenly
samples.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md:1029` documents `sheets.cells.get` on a doc as exit 1 with code `TYPE_MISMATCH`, but `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25` does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`)`, so the backend `code` is discarded and stderr shows `code: "ERROR"`. Related: `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41` reads `(res.data as { error?: { message?: string } })?.error?.message` off an unvalidated body — the cast this change removed elsewhere. Pre-existing rather than introduced here, but now the CLI has two different upstream-error policies for the same backend envelope; the new `forwardUpstreamError`/`isErrorEnvelope` helper is the natural home for both.

samples.summary: Bodies shaped `{error:{message}}` (no `code`) now lose the upstream message that used to be forwarded
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:76-85) requires a string `code`, so a body like `{ "error": { "message": "workspace suspended" } }` — previously forwarded verbatim by the truthiness test — now collapses to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 403"}}` and the upstream prose is dropped. I could only find one backend producer of the envelope (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42-47`, which does set `code`), so no in-repo caller is confirmed broken; a reverse proxy, gateway, or older server version between CLI and backend would be. Retaining `error.message` in the rethrown message when present would keep the diagnostic without weakening the guard.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The centralised envelope guard exists (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:76-110, isErrorEnvelope/forwardUpstreamError) and is wired only to the six content sites (commands/docs.ts:197,249; commands/slides.ts:154,197; commands/notes.ts:148,195). The four sites named in the finding are present verbatim and bypass it: docs/import.ts:164 (also :194,:211), slides/import.ts:194 (also :237,:254), notes/import.ts:159 (also :188,:212), files/upload.ts:217 — plus an unnamed fifth at files/download.ts:57. The bypass is mechanically real: HttpClient.request does `data = await res.json().catch(() => null)` (http-client.ts:184) and uploadFileDocument the same (http-client.ts:248), so a Nest/Express 404/500 body `{message, error:"Not Found", statusCode}` is non-null, skips the `??` fallback, and is printed verbatim with `error.code === undefined` — precisely the case formatter.ts:71-74 says the guard exists to reject, and precisely the case skills/docs-import-docx.md:84 and skills/slides-import-pptx.md:72 tell agents will surface as `HTTP_ERROR`. All paths are reachable from registered commands (commands/docs.ts:338, commands/slides.ts:222, commands/notes.ts:222, commands/files.ts:32). No guard elsewhere normalises these bodies, so `already-guarded` does not apply, and the code is exactly as described so `not-present` does not apply. The task doc's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:41-45) claim other paths "do not have this pattern", which is factually false for these sites and is not a guard; a task-doc scope statement cannot narrow this lens. In lane for blast-radius: an invariant/contract other consumers assume, violated at entry points invisible in the diff.
